remaining_tasks.name: The b-layer is modelled as if it were the t-layer. ParityText's regex /(\d+)([-+?])/g matches only a number followed by a sign, so in 'b2-1+' it emits {kind:'stereo', atom:1} and swallows the leading 2 as inert text. But b2-1+ names a DOUBLE BOND between atoms 2 and 1, not a stereocentre at atom 1. Diagnosed from src/components/LayerText.tsx:426-453, never fixed. Fixture: InChI=1S/C4H4O4/c5-3(6)1-2-4(7)8/h1-2H,(H,5,6)(H,7,8)/b2-1+ (fumaric acid).

decisions.decision: --line stays soft at 1.37:1; a separate --line-control token carries the 3:1 boundary
decisions.rationale: WCAG 1.4.11 covers UI components, not decorative container edges. Darkening --line globally would have coarsened 25 container borders across a deliberately soft page for no standards gain, and darkening the pills' --line FILL instead would have broken --ink-soft's 4.5:1 on top of it. Asserted both ways in tokenContrast.test.ts, including that --line is deliberately under 3:1.

decisions.decision: Absent legend rows keep their text at 4.5:1 and are separated by shape and weight instead
decisions.rationale: They are focusable and open their own explanation card, so they are ACTIVE controls and WCAG 1.4.3's incidental-text exception does not apply. --ink-faint is 5.20:1 on the card; the lightest AA-legal value is L=0.56 at 4.58:1, a barely perceptible gain for the last of the headroom. Spent the effect on a hollow swatch ring and a weight step instead.

decisions.decision: The Dockerfile now gzips .wasm, overriding a documented decision in two files
decisions.rationale: Both files excluded .wasm to protect streaming compilation, which cost nothing while the wasm was inlined and never fetched. Fetched for real, the exclusion would ship 11.8MB uncompressed - worse than the 7.17MB of gzipped base64 it replaces. Content-Encoding is transfer-level: the browser inflates before WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming reads, and Content-Type is what streaming needs. Verified the emitted worker does use instantiateStreaming with an ArrayBuffer fallback.

decisions.decision: Touch target size follows (pointer: coarse); layout still follows max-width
decisions.rationale: Keying targets to width served a 1024px iPad 32px mouse pills and a 700px desktop window 44px finger pills - both backwards. Enumerated per control rather than as one `button` base rule, because the InChI layer chunks are inline spans carrying role=button from lib/keyboardProps and a blanket min-height would inflate the line boxes of the string the page is about.

context_notes: Three process failures this session, all worth carrying. (1) I ran `git checkout` on an uncommitted file to undo a mutation test and wiped a whole pass's edits to KetcherPanel.tsx. Mutation-test against a scratch copy, or commit first. (2) My hunk-staging helper used git diff -U3 while I had inspected at -U0, so adjacent hunks from different logical changes merged and I committed a broken commit 6 (tsc: Cannot find name 'show'). Caught only because I verified each commit in isolation by stashing the remainder - do that, always. (3) My own audit's grep missed three controls with `border: none` and a --line fill, and separately flagged .mol-item as dead CSS when it is built by string concatenation at KetcherPanel.tsx:101 - deleting on that evidence would have stripped the preset picker's styling. Verify an 'unused' claim against how the thing is actually constructed. Carried forward and repeatedly useful: a guard is worthless until you try to break it. Every new guard this session was mutation-tested by reverting the fix and watching the test fail; that is how the segmentBonds comma regression and the two staging errors were caught.
